thread:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT 6325009876 - multiple hosted runtime nodes reporting KV cache OOMs in us-west-2. Auto-page to #incidents.

maya: seeing steady spike in kvheap on runtime-nodes-7..12, GC not keeping up. memory usage jumping from ~42% -> 98% over ~3m. logs show repeated 'kvmap: insert failed: OOM' loops.

sanjay: noticing pattern: long user sessions with huge open contexts (chat apps resuming with previous context) — prefix amplification. Batching has also increased; saw batch_window_ms jumped after last canary.

ophelia: ^ that's the canary we rolled at 04:12 UTC — it lowered batch window to 12ms but accidentally increased continuous prefetch multiplier. suspect prefetch depth growth + continuous batching combining to create ghost windows.

liam: can we throttle prefetch immediately? if we cap prefetch depth per session we should stop growth. I'm going to push quick hotpatch to the control plane to force per-session cap.

maya: agree. also we should put rate limit on long sessions from hosted tier while we mitigate. customer-impact: some orgs report elevated 5xx on generation endpoints, and latency spikes > 10s for long prompts. opened support ticket SR-9921.

sanjay: applying runtime config patch now to disable continuous prefetch for hosted-prod pool and set conservative defaults.

sanjay: runbook actions:
1) set /service/runtime/prefetch/enabled = false
2) set /service/runtime/prefetch/max_per_session = 256
3) set /service/runtime/kvcache/max_keys = 500000
4) revert canary that increased prefetch multiplier

ophelia: executing step1..3 via deploy tool. command: `deployctl apply -f - <<EOF\nservice: runtime\nprefetch:\n  enabled: false\n  max_per_session: 256\nkvcache:\n  max_keys: 500000\nEOF`

infra-bot: rollout started: prefetch toggle -> staged to hosted-prod pool (12 pods). progress: 0/12 updated.

maya: hitting the most critical part: we need to avoid mass restarts that would evict other caches. stage updates one node at a time, give 2m between nodes.

sanjay: confirmed. staging cadence set to 1 node every 90s. initiating.

support-bot: customer-impact update: 6 customers with >20% error increase, 42 customers with latency >3s. No data exfiltration. Support will post templated status update after triage.

liam: monitoring metrics: kv_heap_count (per-node) trending down on updated nodes, batch_size distribution narrowing. but a couple nodes still show high resident set from payloads that already triggered OOMs.

maya: created targeted scrub job to evict oversized session keys older than 24h on impacted nodes: `kvtidy --older-than 24h --max-keys 1000 --node runtime-node-9` (dry-run first)

ophelia: started dry-run on node-9; results look safe. executing sweep in 30s.

infra-bot: node-9 sweep complete: reclaimed ~1.3GB of KV memory, 12k keys evicted. no restart.

sanjay: propagation now 6/12 nodes updated. errors on gen endpoints dropping from 18% -> 7% in the last 3m. latency p50 improved from 480ms -> 220ms for normal prompts.

maya: still saw one reproducible case: a resumed conversation with repeated image captions + long code blocks caused a single session to create 1.2M kv-entries. need an additional guard to reject single-session keys > 200k.

liam: adding guard: `if session_keys > 200000 -> mark session read-only + emit alert`. rolling to hosted-prod as follow-up patch.

support-bot: posted to customers: "We experienced a KV cache-related incident impacting generation latency and errors for some hosted customers. Mitigation in progress; we are throttling large sessions and applying fixes. Follow-ups to come." :white_check_mark:

ophelia: propagation complete: 12/12 nodes updated. metrics look stable. no further OOMs in last 8m.

maya: action items:
- postmortem owner: @maya
- follow-up hotfix to add per-session hard cap (PR submitted by @liam)
- e2e test to include long resumed-session scenario
- telemetry: add alert for session_key_count > 100k

sanjay: leaving on-call handoff at 08:30 UTC to @ophelia — postmortem and cleanup to continue tomorrow. tagging incident severity: Sev2; customer comms scheduled.

liam: adding small note: we should audit the last canary to ensure prefetch multiplier change wasn't applied to other clusters. filing TKT-1107.

pagerduty-bot: On-call handoff: sanjay -> ophelia at 08:30 UTC. Reminder: check `kv_heap_count` and `session_key_count` alerts.

maya: thanks team. I'll start the postmortem doc and run the eval suite to catch regressions in continuous prefetch behavior. closing channel when postmortem ready. :pray:

ophelia: acknowledged. monitoring for next 2 hours then will relax throttles if stable. :eyes:
